paper.title: MAPL: Multi-Objective Preference Learning for Robot Locomotion
paper.source_version: arXiv v1, submitted 2026-06-24; exact 3,698,572-byte source archive SHA-256 8ce6faab1e094823dab7fcf8c4ced43ba939c4c326a8ea15e4dbf53f93bf4115. Official CAMP Lab public record pinned to commit 7624ed21aba13a83682d50c6b9b8f8399da3c37c; its 4,223,359-byte PDF SHA-256 is 31ba53f8f5497f1c67ac505b2f442ad1532af17df6a9fca0840796e0288b507b. No MAPL implementation is listed there; checked 2026-08-30.

decision_relevance.why_admitted: MAPL decomposes a language-specified locomotion objective into separately elicited preferences, learns a multi-head neural reward, and exposes explicit aggregation weights and ablations. This directly informs task-reward artifact design and a possible language-to-reward interface, while its online reward-model updates, overlapping evaluation reward, and incomplete versioning define strict boundaries for Sam's fixed-trainer protocol.
not_evidence_for: Reference selection, reference composition, transition guards, recovery coverage, mode discovery, or oracle logic
An immutable task-reward artifact held fixed throughout one policy-training run
Executable or auditable reward code generation
Permission to replace Sam's frozen tracking reward with MAPL's whole-locomotion velocity, stability, and smoothness reward
Permission to change terrain curriculum, scene generation, policy architecture, or PPO settings inside Sam's initial reward search
Reliable human steering, because the paper evaluates fixed author-written prompts and AI rankings rather than human edits
Elimination of all reward engineering, because aggregation weights are manual and terrain-dependent and rubrics contain embodiment-specific quantities
Improvement on an untouched reward-independent objective evaluator
Policy invariance of the undiscounted score-difference reward under gamma 0.99 or across episode resets
Hardware transfer, another robot embodiment, another trainer, or another observation/action contract
Exact reproducibility without released MAPL code and pinned simulator, RL-library, and LLM versions
Numerical headline return differences or statistical significance beyond the plotted curves

mechanisms.name: Objective-wise LLM preference generation
mechanisms.description: Trajectory pairs are downsampled and presented to separate velocity, stability, and smoothness rubrics; the LLM ranks each objective independently, with repeated queries optionally reduced by majority vote.

mechanisms.name: Shared Transformer with objective heads
mechanisms.description: A shared Transformer backbone has one state-score output head for each of velocity, stability, and smoothness and is trained from objective-specific Bradley-Terry pairwise losses.

mechanisms.name: Manual linear objective aggregation
mechanisms.description: Three objective scores are linearly combined using a manually selected lambda vector; the smoothness weight differs between flat/wave and stair/obstacle terrains.

mechanisms.name: Consecutive-score difference reward
mechanisms.description: The scalar policy reward is the aggregate preference score at the current state minus its score at the previous state, rather than the raw learned score.

mechanisms.name: Alternating reward-model and policy updates
mechanisms.description: Policy rollouts refresh preference data and the scoring model at one-hundredth the policy-update frequency while PPO continually consumes the current learned score-difference reward.

mechanisms.name: Natural-language reward specification interface
mechanisms.description: Author-written language rubrics select trajectory channels and comparison rules without an explicit reward equation; this is a candidate interface for steering reward proposals, not evidence that human steering was tested.

parameters.name: preference_objectives
parameters.context: The same three semantic objectives are used across all four terrains, with a separate output head and objective-specific prompt for each.

parameters.name: downsampled_states_per_trajectory
parameters.context: Exact continuous-state count in each appendix preference prompt; the original trajectory horizon and sampling cadence are not reported.

parameters.name: trajectory_pairs_per_llm_request
parameters.context: Each objective-specific prompt asks for one array containing labels for twenty independently judged pairs.

parameters.name: preference_label_encodings
parameters.context: The paper does not state how prompt tie label 2 is converted to the theoretical 0.5 target.

parameters.name: velocity_prompt_feature_shapes
parameters.context: Velocity preference input and its explicit decision priority; trot foot-contact consistency is only a tiebreaker after tracking is close.

parameters.name: stability_prompt_parameters
parameters.context: Embodiment-specific stability preference inputs and target.

parameters.name: smoothness_prompt_feature_shapes
parameters.context: Smoothness inputs; the rubric makes a clear stumble dominate a small action-smoothness advantage.

parameters.name: scoring_model_update_frequency_ratio
parameters.context: The scoring model is updated one hundred times less frequently than the policy.

parameters.name: preference_aggregation_weights
parameters.context: Manually specified terrain-dependent lambda ratios used in the main experiments.

parameters.name: policy_reward_formula
parameters.context: Difference of consecutive aggregate learned scores; no gamma multiplier or episode-boundary convention is specified.

parameters.name: default_llm_name
parameters.context: Used for all rankings unless otherwise specified; no exact snapshot, provider settings, temperature, or decoding seed is reported.

parameters.name: llm_backbone_ablation_names
parameters.context: Three-seed Plane comparison of the velocity preference model; exact provider snapshots and decoding configurations are not reported.

parameters.name: main_preference_training_pairs
parameters.units: trajectory pairs per preference reward model
parameters.context: Main locomotion-policy comparison.

parameters.name: component_ablation_training_pairs
parameters.units: trajectory pairs per preference reward model
parameters.context: Same pair count for each objective subset in the component ablation.

parameters.name: trajectory_buffer_sensitivity_sizes
parameters.context: Plane-environment sensitivity study; one thousand gives the highest plotted expert evaluation reward and five hundred remains competitive.

parameters.name: llm_query_repeat_sensitivity
parameters.context: Plane-environment majority-vote sensitivity; curves are reported as nearly identical at three or more repeats, but the main default is not stated.

parameters.name: reward_transformer_hyperparameters
parameters.context: Manually tuned preference scoring model.

parameters.name: reward_transformer_learning_rate_schedule
parameters.context: Learning-rate value paired with the epoch at which the appendix says it is applied.

parameters.name: shared_ppo_hyperparameters
parameters.context: PPO settings reported for every environment and baseline.

parameters.name: main_policy_seeds
parameters.units: independent random seeds per reward method
parameters.context: Main policy comparison and score-difference ablation.

parameters.name: ablation_policy_seeds
parameters.context: Component, LLM-backbone, trajectory-buffer, query-count, and lambda sensitivity studies.

parameters.name: plotted_training_iterations_by_terrain
parameters.context: Main Figure 3 x-axis horizons; methods are compared to the same horizon within each terrain.

parameters.name: evaluation_velocity_reward_scales
parameters.context: Denominators in the Gaussian linear and angular velocity evaluation rewards.

parameters.name: expert_reward_weights
parameters.context: Hand-designed expert reward used as a PPO baseline and as the basis of several evaluation and ranking comparisons.

parameters.name: velocity_error_command_range
parameters.units: m/s for linear commands; rad/s for yaw command
parameters.context: Forward-velocity error evaluation across every terrain.

parameters.name: velocity_error_rollout_protocol
parameters.context: Velocity errors are computed from interval-averaged velocities.

parameters.name: preference_query_ranking_accuracy_percent
parameters.context: Accuracy against expert-reward rankings over one hundred trajectory pairs; overall and decomposed-objective columns are not directly interchangeable.

failure_modes.name: Single and incomplete objective sets fail
failure_modes.description: Velocity-only, stability-only, and smoothness-only rewards converge at low or near-zero expert evaluation return; velocity plus stability also fails to improve, and the full three-term reward is reported near twice the best two-term variant.

failure_modes.name: Linear aggregation misses objective interactions
failure_modes.description: The authors identify linear scalarization as interpretable but potentially insufficient for interactions among locomotion objectives.

failure_modes.name: Score difference does not help every reward model
failure_modes.description: Removing score difference degrades MAPL, but adding the same operation to the LLM Reward and LAPP baselines can cause early plateaus or unstable training.

failure_modes.name: Stochastic LLM rankings
failure_modes.description: Repeated calls can disagree; majority voting is the mitigation, although the Plane sensitivity study reports little benefit beyond three queries.

failure_modes.name: Reward changes inside policy training
failure_modes.description: The preference model is refreshed from current-policy rollouts while PPO continues, so MAPL is not a comparison of one immutable task reward per complete training run.

failure_modes.name: Evaluation overlaps reward design
failure_modes.description: Expert velocity rewards form the reported evaluation return and expert-reward decompositions define ranking ground truth, so these studies do not supply an untouched reward-independent objective metric.

failure_modes.name: Tie encoding is unresolved
failure_modes.description: The prompts emit 2 for a tie while the theoretical label is 0.5; no official implementation is available to establish the conversion.

failure_modes.name: Runtime reward-model input is underspecified
failure_modes.description: Equations score a state, but smoothness supervision depends on action changes and stumble history; v1 does not give the exact feature tensor or online history construction.

failure_modes.name: Discount and reset semantics are unspecified
failure_modes.description: The score difference omits a gamma factor even though PPO uses gamma 0.99, and the paper gives no terminal-state or episode-reset convention or invariance argument.

failure_modes.name: Public reproduction identity is incomplete
failure_modes.description: The paper names Isaac Gym, Legged-Gym, RSL-RL, and GPT-5-mini without versions or commits; the pinned official lab registry exposes a PDF but no MAPL implementation.

failure_modes.name: Simulation-only and figure-only headline evidence
failure_modes.description: All reported policies use one simulated Unitree Go2 setup; headline returns are smoothed curves with standard errors rather than tabulated effect sizes or hypothesis tests.

evaluation.name: Four-terrain Unitree Go2 benchmark
evaluation.description: Five policy seeds per reward method are trained in Isaac Gym/Legged-Gym on Plane, Wave, Stair, and Obstacle tasks with shared PPO settings and terrain-specific iteration horizons.

evaluation.name: Expert-reward and difficulty-weighted evaluation
evaluation.description: Gaussian linear and angular command-tracking terms, and on uneven terrain a difficulty multiplier, measure policy performance; the broader expert reward is also the PPO upper-bound baseline.

evaluation.name: Preference-component ablation
evaluation.description: Three-seed runs compare every single objective, all pairs, and all three objectives using two thousand trajectory pairs per reward model.

evaluation.name: Trajectory-buffer and LLM-query sensitivity
evaluation.description: Plane experiments vary trajectory count and repeated rankings; five hundred trajectories remain competitive, and three or more queries produce nearly identical curves.

evaluation.name: Score-difference ablation
evaluation.description: Five-seed learning curves compare MAPL, LLM Reward, and LAPP with and without consecutive-score difference on all four terrains.

evaluation.name: Physical-state distribution and lambda sensitivity
evaluation.description: Plane rollouts compare base-height, roll, and pitch distributions across reward methods, and three-seed runs vary each objective weight among 0.1, 1.0, and 1.5.

evaluation.name: Forward-velocity tracking error
evaluation.description: With lateral and yaw commands set to zero, forward command varies from 0.4 to 1.0 m/s; velocities are averaged over twenty-step intervals in a five-hundred-step rollout.

evaluation.name: Expert-reward ranking accuracy
evaluation.description: One hundred trajectory pairs compare overall and objective-specific LLM ranking strategies against full or decomposed expert-reward orderings.

evidence.claim: The active record has one version, submitted 24 June 2026, with title, four authors, cs.RO classification, and arXiv DOI.

MAPL alternates preference-data/scorer updates with policy updates; trajectories receive pairwise labels, a Bradley-Terry loss trains scores, and policy reward is the difference between current and previous scores.
Velocity tracking, stability, and smoothness are the three natural-language criteria reused without terrain-specific prompt modifications.
Objectives are ranked separately, repeated queries are majority-voted, a shared Transformer has one head per objective, and the scoring model updates one hundred times more slowly than the policy.
Objective scores use a manually specified linear lambda aggregation, and the policy reward subtracts the previous aggregate score from the current score.

evidence.locator: Section V-A, Equations 7-9 and Table I
evidence.claim: All experiments use simulated Unitree Go2 in four Isaac Gym/Legged-Gym terrains; evaluation uses Gaussian velocity rewards, a ten-term expert reward, curriculum, and difficulty weighting.
The baselines share PPO/RSL-RL, LAPP is modified to remove environment reward, lambda ratios are 1.5/1.0/0.1 or 1.5/1.0/0.25 by terrain, and rankings default to the named GPT-5-mini model.

Each main preference reward model uses five hundred trajectory pairs, each reward method trains five seeded policies, and plotted curves qualitatively match or exceed expert reward at terrain-specific horizons.

Three-seed Figure 4 covers component, LLM-backbone, buffer, and query ablations; the component study uses two thousand trajectory pairs, incomplete objective sets underperform, and the full reward is reported near twice the best two-term result.

Plane sensitivity studies test 100/200/500/1000 trajectories and 1/3/5/7 repeated rankings; one thousand trajectories is highest, five hundred remains competitive, and three or more query curves are nearly identical.
Five-seed ablations report that score difference improves MAPL on all terrains but can make LLM Reward or LAPP plateau early or train unstably.

evidence.locator: Sections V-F and V-G, Figures 7 and 8
evidence.claim: Plane physical-state distributions are sampled from twenty steps in sixteen random objectives; three-seed lambda sensitivity compares 0.1, 1.0, and 1.5 for each objective.

Forward command varies from 0.4 to 1.0 m/s with zero lateral and yaw commands; velocities use twenty-step averages in a five-hundred-step rollout, and MAPL has the lowest plotted error on every terrain.

On one hundred trajectory pairs, MAPL objective ranking accuracy is 88/76/98 percent for velocity/stability/smoothness; MOSQ is 67/67/98 percent and overall SOSQ/LAPP are 63/68 percent against expert-reward ground truth.
The paper identifies linear aggregation as potentially inexpressive for objective interactions and leaves multimodal feedback and loco-manipulation to future work.
The manually tuned reward Transformer has embedding 256, two layers, four heads, feedforward 512, dropout 0.1, batch 32, eighty epochs, and the reported three-point learning-rate schedule.
The paper reports batch and minibatch sizes, five PPO epochs, clip 0.2, entropy 0.01, gamma 0.99, GAE lambda 0.95, target KL 0.01, and adaptive learning rate for every environment.
The velocity prompt fixes six-state feature shapes, a 3:1 linear-to-yaw priority, conditional trot preference, twenty pairs per request, and 0/1/2 output labels.
The stability prompt uses six-state base height, vertical velocity, and roll/pitch velocity features and specifies a 0.34-meter base-height target.
The smoothness prompt uses six-state summed action-change and stumble inputs and prioritizes clear stumble avoidance over small action-smoothness differences.
